thesis: Credential theft incidents surged significantly while high severity attacks rose, marking a shift from traditional ransomware threats to more acute credential-focused risks targeting the energy sector.

themes.title: Credential Theft Emerges as Primary Risk
themes.summary: Incidents of credential theft rose sharply compared to last year, indicating a critical shift in attacker tactics that requires immediate monitoring.

themes.title: New Malware Dominates the Threat Landscape
themes.summary: A new malware family became the leading threat detected, while other attack types showed varying levels of decline or growth.

themes.title: Energy Sector Faces Intensified Geographic Attacks
themes.summary: The energy sector absorbed the highest volume of attack traffic while new sources like Brazil emerged as major contributors to malicious traffic.

sections.title: Product performance
sections.goal: Review how specific security products blocked various attack types and their year-over-year volume changes.

sections.title: Top malware
sections.goal: Identify the ranking of most detected malware families and note which new families entered the threat catalog.

sections.title: Source countries
sections.goal: Analyze the geographic origins of attack traffic and observe how country rankings shifted during the reporting period.

sections.title: Trends
sections.goal: Examine monthly patterns, changes in attack type popularity across products, and the industries most targeted by threats.

sections.title: Recommendations
sections.goal: Review specific security actions to take against rising high severity threats, new malware families, and targeted sectors.
